scenario: 面试官给了一个新系统，只说功能没给访问模式，你要当场定下用哪种存储结构。
q: 选存储引擎 / 索引结构时，最该先问自己的一组问题是？
options: 内存/磁盘 · 读/写 · 等值/范围 · 超不超 RAM · 要不要持久化
用什么编程语言 · 团队规模多大 · 预算上限是多少
先站队决定要用 NoSQL 还是 SQL，再把它的所有特性都从头到尾硬背下来
无脑默认使用 Postgres 存储所有数据，从来不做针对性分析
why: 选存储结构靠五问：内存/磁盘、读/写、等值/范围、超不超 RAM、要不要持久化。答案通常落在哈希表、B 树、LSM 树三选一，细节见下表。
why_en: You don't memorize storage choices — you ask five questions: (1) memory or disk, (2) read- or write-heavy, (3) exact-match only or need range/sort, (4) will data exceed RAM, (5) need durability. Three core structures: hash table (O(1) exact-match, in-memory), B-tree (read-optimized + range, on disk), and LSM tree (write-optimized, log-structured). This is the master map behind every index/engine card.

rows: O(1) 只等值·无范围（内存）
读优化·原地更新·范围+排序（磁盘）
写优化·顺序写+后台合并

q_en: When choosing a storage engine or index structure, what's the first set of questions to ask?
scenario_en: In an interview you're handed a new system with features but no access pattern, and you have to settle on a storage structure on the spot.
options_en: Memory or disk · read- or write-heavy · equality or range · fits in RAM or not · needs durability or not.
What programming language to use, how big the team is, what the budget is.
First pick a side, NoSQL vs SQL, then memorize every one of its features by rote from start to end.
Default to storing everything in Postgres blindly, never analyzing the access pattern at all.
optionExplanations: 对，这五个问题直接决定该选哪种存储结构：内存还是磁盘、读写比例、等值还是范围、是否超 RAM、要不要持久化。
语言、团队规模、预算是工程管理变量，不影响该选哈希表、B 树还是 LSM——真正决定因素是数据访问模式。
先站队 NoSQL/SQL 再硬背特性是本末倒置：存储结构该看访问模式，不是先选阵营。
跳过分析直接默认 Postgres：它默认走 B 树，遇到全内存等值查找或海量写入摄入这类场景就不是最优选择。
optionExplanations_en: Right — these five questions directly decide which storage structure to use: memory vs disk, read/write mix, equality vs range, fits in RAM, needs durability.
Language, team size, and budget are engineering-management variables — they don't decide between a hash table, B-tree, or LSM tree; the access pattern does.
Picking NoSQL vs SQL first and memorizing its features backwards is the wrong order — the structure choice should follow the access pattern, not a camp.
Skipping analysis and defaulting to Postgres: it defaults to B-tree, which isn't optimal for pure in-memory equality lookups or extreme write ingestion.

scenario: 用户表 100 万行、每页约 100 行，登录要按 email 查一条记录，而 email 列上没有索引。
q: 没有索引时，按 email 在百万行的表里找一个用户，为什么慢？
options: 数据库锁竞争太激烈，大量读写请求互相阻塞排队
SQL 解析和优化器耗时太长
无索引只能逐页扫描整张表，每页都要读盘检查
网络往返次数太多，客户端反复请求
why: 无索引时数据库别无选择，只能把每一页数据依次读进内存逐行检查；上百万页就是上百万次相对缓慢的磁盘读，只为找一条记录。
why_en: Without an index the database must sequentially scan every page, loading each from disk into memory, which means millions of slow disk reads to find one record.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Query email"] --> B["Full table scan"]
  B --> C["Check every row"]
  C --> D["Return match"]
options_en: Lock contention is too severe — many read and write requests block and queue against each other.
SQL parsing and query planning take too long.
Without an index it must scan every page sequentially, reading each into memory to check.
There are too many network round trips between client and server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的、独立于主表的结构化数据路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a separate structured data path maintained purely to speed up lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言，用来查询和操作关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, used to query and manipulate relational databases.

q_en: Why is finding a user by email slow in a million-row table with no index?
scenario_en: A users table has a million rows at roughly a hundred rows per page, and login looks a user up by email with no index on that column.
optionExplanations: 锁竞争影响的是并发写入的等待时间，不会让单条查询本身慢到要扫全表。
SQL 解析和选执行计划确实耗时，但那是毫秒级开销，远不是全表扫描慢的主因。
对，没有索引数据库就只能按物理顺序把每一页读进内存逐行核对，页数越多越慢。
一次请求只有一次网络往返，跟数据库内部要扫多少页无关。
optionExplanations_en: Lock contention affects how long concurrent writers wait, not why a single lookup itself has to scan the whole table.
SQL parsing and planning do cost time, but that's a millisecond-level overhead, not the reason a full scan is slow.
Right — with no index the database has no shortcut, so it loads every page in physical order and checks each row; more pages means more time.
A single request makes one round trip; that has nothing to do with how many pages the database scans internally.

scenario: Postgres 的 users 表主键 B 树已经建好；现在问行数据本身躺在磁盘的哪种文件里。
q: 主表数据在磁盘上的典型存储形式是？
options: 堆文件（heap file）：行按写入顺序堆放，没有特定排序
始终严格按主键排序的有序文件，每次写入都要维持排序位置并挪动后续行
哈希桶数组，把行按主键的哈希值分散存放各处
按列存储的列式压缩数据块，而非按行组织存储
why: 选堆文件。这里问主表数据，不是主键索引：行通常堆在数据页里；主键 B-tree 另存并指向这些行。
why_en: Choose heap file. This asks about table data, not the primary-key index: rows usually live in heap pages, while a separate primary-key B-tree points to them.
whenOtherWins: 例外：InnoDB 用 clustered index；Postgres 常见是 heap table + separate index。
options_en: A heap file: rows pile up in write order, with no particular sort order.
An always-sorted file strictly ordered by primary key, where every write must maintain sort position and shift the following rows.
A hash bucket array that scatters rows across buckets based on the primary key's hash value.
Column-oriented compressed data blocks, organized by column rather than by row.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    T["table heap pages\nrows in write order"]
    I["primary-key B-tree\nsorted keys"] --> T
    Q["WHERE id = 42"] --> I
    T --> R["row data"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 没有特定顺序的行集合，数据按写入先后堆放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heap file is an unordered collection of rows stored in the order they were written.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识一行数据的列或列组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A primary key is the column or columns that uniquely identify each row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引顺序就是主表数据顺序的存储方式，MySQL InnoDB 的主键就是典型例子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clustered index stores table rows in the same order as the index; MySQL InnoDB primary keys are the classic example.

q_en: How is the main table data usually stored on disk?
scenario_en: A Postgres users table already has its primary-key B-tree built; the question is what kind of file the row data itself sits in on disk.
optionExplanations: 对，主表数据默认堆放在数据页里、没有排序要求，插入只管追加；真正维持顺序的是另外那棵主键 B 树索引。
这其实是聚簇索引（clustered index）的做法，如 InnoDB；本题问的是更常见的默认存储：堆文件。
哈希桶数组是哈希索引的结构，不是主表数据默认的存放方式。
列式存储是分析型数据库（如 ClickHouse）的组织方式，OLTP 主表默认按行存放在堆文件里。
optionExplanations_en: Right — by default, rows just pile into heap pages with no order; insert simply appends. Keeping order is the separate primary-key B-tree's job.
That's actually a clustered index, like InnoDB uses; this question asks about the more common default: an unordered heap file.
A hash bucket array is how a hash index is structured, not how the main table's rows are stored by default.
Columnar storage is how analytical databases like ClickHouse organize data; OLTP tables default to row-oriented heap files.

scenario: 一条 SELECT 要读 users 表的 3 个数据页，数据在 SSD 上，CPU 要逐行比较字段值。
q: 为什么每次数据库查询都绕不开「从磁盘加载到内存」这一步？
options: 因为内存容量实在太小，根本没办法长期放下任何需要持久化的数据
数据落在磁盘上，只有搬进内存（RAM）才能被 CPU 处理
因为磁盘硬件本身设计上完全不支持随机读取
为了保证事务的隔离性级别能够真正达标
why: 数据落在磁盘（如今多为 SSD），而 CPU 只能处理内存里的数据，所以每个查询都要把相关页从磁盘搬进 RAM。索引的价值就是减少要搬的页数。
why_en: Data lives on disk but can only be processed in memory, so every query loads pages from disk into RAM, and indexes minimize how many pages that takes.
options_en: Because memory is far too small to hold, long-term, any data that needs to be persisted.
Data sits on disk, and only once it's pulled into memory (RAM) can the CPU process it.
Because disk hardware itself is designed to not support random reads at all.
To make sure the transaction isolation level genuinely meets its guarantee.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机存取内存，CPU 能直接处理的高速易失存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, the fast volatile storage the CPU can directly process.

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器，执行程序指令的核心部件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, executes program instructions.

q_en: Why does every database query have to load data from disk into memory?
scenario_en: One SELECT needs three data pages from the users table; the data lives on SSD and the CPU has to compare field values row by row.
optionExplanations: 夸大了：内存确实放不下全部数据，但真正原因是处理器只能操作装在内存里的东西，磁盘上的页得先搬进 RAM 才能被读到。
对，处理器只能读写内存里的内容；磁盘上的页得先被搬进 RAM 才能被访问，这一步谁都跳不过。
现代 SSD/HDD 都支持随机读取，只是比顺序读慢，不是不支持。
隔离级别管的是并发事务互相看不看得到彼此的修改，跟数据要不要从磁盘搬进内存无关。
optionExplanations_en: Overstated — memory can't hold everything, but the real reason is a processor can only operate on what is already loaded into memory; a disk page has to be pulled in first.
Right — the processor can only read and write content sitting in memory; a page on disk always has to be pulled into RAM first, no way around it.
Modern SSDs and HDDs both support random reads — they're just slower than sequential reads, not unsupported.
Isolation levels control whether concurrent transactions see each other's uncommitted changes; unrelated to moving data from disk into memory.

scenario: 机器全是 SSD，有人主张干脆去掉索引、让查询走全表扫描，说反正 SSD 没有寻道代价。
q: 关于 SSD 上「随机访问 vs 顺序访问」，正确的说法是？
options: SSD 上随机访问和顺序访问的速度完全一样，两者之间没有任何差距
SSD 上随机访问的速度反而比顺序访问还要更快
只有传统机械硬盘 HDD 才会存在两者的速度差距
SSD 上随机访问仍明显慢于顺序访问——常见误解是这差距已消失
why: 常见误解是 SSD 抹平了差距：其实差距只是比 HDD 小，随机访问依然明显更慢；HDD 上差距更悬殊，所以合理建索引至关重要。
why_en: Even on SSDs random access is still significantly slower than sequential access, a smaller gap than on HDDs but a very real one.
options_en: On an SSD, random and sequential access are exactly the same speed, with no gap between them whatsoever.
On an SSD, random access is actually faster than sequential access.
Only traditional mechanical HDDs have a speed gap between the two.
SSD random access is still noticeably slower than sequential — the common misconception is that this gap has vanished.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，无机械部件的闪存存储介质，随机访问比机械硬盘快得多但仍慢于顺序访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSD stands for Solid State Drive, flash-based storage much faster at random access than spinning disks but still slower than sequential access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机械硬盘，靠磁头寻道读写的存储介质，随机访问比顺序访问慢得多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HDD stands for Hard Disk Drive, mechanical storage where random access is much slower than sequential access due to seek time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按不连续、不可预测的顺序读写数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random access means reading or writing data in a non-sequential, unpredictable order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按连续顺序读写数据，通常更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential access means reading or writing data in contiguous order, which is usually faster.

q_en: What is true about random access versus sequential access on SSDs?
scenario_en: The machines are all SSD, and someone argues you can drop the index and just full-scan, since SSDs supposedly have no seek penalty.
optionExplanations: SSD 确实比 HDD 抹平了很多差距，但没抹平到「完全一样」；随机访问仍要付出额外开销（如闪存页/块管理）。
说反了：无论 SSD 还是 HDD，顺序访问都比随机访问快，只是 SSD 上差距被缩小了。
HDD 上差距确实更悬殊（机械寻道），但 SSD 上的差距只是变小，并没有消失。
对，SSD 只是把差距从 HDD 的数量级缩小到更小但依然明显的程度，索引依然重要。
optionExplanations_en: SSDs do narrow the gap versus HDDs, but not to zero — random access still pays extra overhead like flash page/block management.
Backwards — on both SSD and HDD, sequential beats random; SSDs just shrink that gap, they don't invert it.
The gap is bigger on HDDs because of mechanical seek time, but on SSDs it only shrinks — it doesn't disappear.
Right — SSDs shrink the gap from HDD-scale down to something smaller but still real, which is why indexing still matters.

scenario: 同一张 1 亿行的表，加上 email 索引后单条查询从 2 秒降到 2 毫秒，要解释这 1000 倍差距。
q: 索引让查询变快的本质机制是什么？
options: 把所有数据都压缩得更小，从而大幅节省磁盘空间的占用面积
提供结构化路径，直接指出数据在哪些页，减少要读的页数
把整张表完整地常驻内存，永远都不用碰磁盘
对所有磁盘页做并行扫描，靠多线程来加速查找
why: 索引是为搜索优化的独立数据结构：它告诉你目标数据具体在哪些页，从而不必逐页检查。就像用书的目录直接翻到相关页，而不是一页页找。
why_en: An index is a separate search-optimized structure that tells the database exactly which pages hold the target data, minimizing pages read from storage.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: Compress all the data down smaller, thereby greatly reducing the disk space it occupies.
Provide a structured path that points straight to the pages holding the data, cutting how many pages you read.
Keep the entire table permanently resident in memory, so disk is never touched.
Parallel-scan every disk page at once, using multiple threads to speed up the search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写磁盘的最小单位，典型大小 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A disk page is the smallest unit a database reads or writes on disk, typically eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为加速查找而维护的、独立于主表的结构化数据路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is a separate structured data path maintained purely to speed up lookups.

q_en: What is the core mechanism that makes an index speed up queries?
scenario_en: On the same hundred-million-row table, adding an email index takes a lookup from two seconds to two milliseconds — explain where that thousand-fold gain comes from.
optionExplanations: 索引确实占额外空间，但目的不是压缩主表——它的作用是加速查找，不是省空间。
对，索引本质是一条结构化路径：直接告诉你目标数据落在哪几页，不用逐页翻找。
常驻内存靠的是缓冲池缓存热数据，不是索引的机制；索引本身也要落盘。
普通查询不会靠多线程并行扫全部页来加速，索引靠的是减少要读的页数，不是加并发。
optionExplanations_en: An index does cost extra space, but its purpose isn't shrinking the main table — it speeds up lookups, not saves space.
Right — an index is fundamentally a structured path: it tells you exactly which pages hold the target data, skipping page-by-page hunting.
Staying resident in memory is the buffer pool caching hot pages, not something the index does — indexes live on disk too.
A normal query doesn't get sped up by parallel-scanning every page with more threads; an index works by cutting pages read, not adding concurrency.

scenario: 一张订单表已经有 5 个索引，还想再加 3 个，而写入 TPS 已经开始往下掉。
q: 索引不是免费的。它的代价包括哪些？（多选）
options: 额外磁盘空间，有时接近原始数据大小
每次插入/更新除了改主表，还要更新表上的每一个索引
多个索引会让一次写操作触发多次磁盘写
有索引后读取一定变慢
why: 索引的三重代价：占磁盘空间、写入时每个索引都要维护、多索引放大写开销。读取恰恰是索引加速的对象，不会因此变慢。
why_en: Indexes cost extra disk space and slow down writes because every insert or update must also update each index, turning one write into several disk writes.
options_en: It costs extra disk space, sometimes nearly as much as the original data.
Every insert or update must update the main table plus every index on it.
Multiple indexes turn a single write into several disk writes.
Reads always get slower once you add an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时同步更新索引结构的开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Index maintenance is the overhead of keeping index structures updated on every write.

q_en: Indexes are not free. What costs do they add? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: An orders table already carries five indexes, three more are proposed, and write throughput has already started dropping.
optionExplanations: 额外磁盘空间是实打实的代价：索引是独立结构，宽字段索引甚至能接近原表大小。
每次 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 除了改主表，还要同步维护这张表上的所有索引，这是写变慢的主因。
索引越多，一次逻辑写就要触发越多次物理磁盘写，写吞吐随索引数量下降。
错——读取正是索引存在的目的，加索引后同类查询通常更快，不会变慢。
optionExplanations_en: Extra disk space is a real cost — an index is a separate structure, and for wide columns it can approach the size of the original table.
Every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE has to update the main table plus every index on it in sync — that's the main reason writes slow down.
The more indexes there are, the more physical disk writes one logical write triggers, so write throughput drops as index count grows.
Wrong — reads are exactly what an index speeds up; after adding an index, matching queries usually get faster, not slower.

scenario: 一张日志表：持续高频插入新记录，但几乎从不查询旧数据。
q: 对这张表，关于索引的正确判断是？
options: 尽量多建索引以防万一，覆盖所有可能出现的查询组合
必须建覆盖索引，避免任何回表
索引可能弊大于利：写多读少，维护开销盖过读收益
建哈希索引就能兼顾写入和查询
why: 写频繁、读极少的表是索引伤害大于收益的经典案例：每次插入都要维护索引，却几乎没人来读。这里少建甚至不建索引才对。
why_en: A write-heavy, rarely-read logging table is the classic case where index maintenance overhead outweighs the benefit.
whenOtherWins: 反过来，读多写少的表（用户资料、商品目录）索引收益远超维护成本，应该按查询模式建索引。
options_en: Add as many indexes as possible just in case, to cover every possible query combination.
You must add a covering index to avoid any table lookup.
Indexes may hurt more than help here: writes dominate, so maintenance overhead outweighs the read benefit.
A hash index alone can satisfy both writing and querying.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 查询收益

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

q_en: For this table, what is the right indexing judgment?
scenario_en: A log table receives high-frequency inserts, but old records are almost never queried.
optionExplanations: 「多建索引防万一」在读多的表上合理，但这张表几乎没人读，多建的索引只会白白拖慢每次插入。
覆盖索引能省回表，但前提是有实际的高频读查询要优化；这张表读极少，谈不上要不要回表。
对，写多读少时索引维护成本盖过查询收益，应该少建甚至不建索引，把插入吞吐留住。
哈希索引能加速等值查找，但解决不了写入侧的索引维护开销——这张表的痛点在写不在读。
optionExplanations_en: "Index everything just in case" makes sense when reads are frequent, but this table is barely read — extra indexes just slow down every insert.
A covering index saves a table lookup, but only pays off with real high-frequency reads to optimize; this table is barely read at all.
Right — when writes dominate and reads are rare, index upkeep outweighs query gains, so build few or no indexes and protect insert throughput.
A hash index would speed up equality lookups, but it doesn't touch the write-side maintenance cost — this table's pain point is writes, not reads.

scenario: 一张只有几百行的小配置表，被问要不要加索引。
q: 最合理的回答是？
options: 可以不加：表太小，索引维护成本可能超过一次顺序扫描
必须加索引，任何表都不能有任何例外情况
加哈希索引，因为它的查找速度永远是最快的
加覆盖索引，提前把所有查询列都塞进去避免任何回表开销
why: 几百行的小表全扫一遍非常便宜，索引的维护与遍历成本反而可能更高。索引的价值随数据量增长才显现。
why_en: For a tiny table a sequential scan is so cheap that maintaining and traversing an index can cost more than it saves.
whenOtherWins: 当表增长到几十万、上百万行且有明确过滤/排序模式时，就该按查询模式补上索引了。
options_en: Skip it: the table is small enough that index upkeep can cost more than one sequential scan.
You must add an index — no table is ever an exception, no matter how small.
Add a hash index, because its lookup speed is always the fastest, period.
Add a covering index, cramming every queried column in up front to avoid any table-lookup cost.
tradeoff: 索引维护成本 vs 顺序扫描成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 从头到尾依次读取表中每一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential scan reads every row of a table from start to end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询需要的所有列都放进索引，让数据库无需回表就能直接从索引返回结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A covering index includes every column a query needs so the database can answer straight from the index without visiting the table.

q_en: What is the most reasonable answer for this tiny table?
scenario_en: You are asked whether to add an index to a tiny configuration table with only a few hundred rows.
optionExplanations: 对，几百行的表全表扫描几乎不花时间，索引反而多一份维护和遍历成本，得不偿失。
「任何表都要加索引」是教条：数据量小到能整表塞进内存时，索引的收益压根体现不出来。
哈希索引等值查找确实快，但这张表本来扫描就快，谈不上要不要用哪种索引。
覆盖索引是为了省回表开销，但小表回表本身就便宜，这个优化在这里没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a full scan of a few hundred rows is nearly free, while an index adds real maintenance and traversal cost; not worth it yet.
"Every table needs an index" is dogma — when the whole table already fits comfortably in memory, an index's benefit never shows up.
A hash index is fast for equality lookups, but this table is already cheap to scan, so index type isn't the issue here.
A covering index exists to skip the extra table lookup, but on a small table that lookup is already cheap, so it buys nothing here.

scenario: 有人否掉新索引，理由是「服务器只有 64GB RAM，每多一个索引内存占用就翻倍」。
q: 索引对内存占用的实际影响，下面哪个判断最准确？
options: 多一个索引，内存占用就会直接翻一倍变大
索引完全不会占用任何一点点内存空间
内存影响是索引所有代价里最致命、最该优先担心的那一个
影响常被夸大：缓冲池管理已很智能，但仍要监控索引使用
why: 内存影响常被夸大：缓冲池是 LRU 缓存，只把热页留在内存，冷索引几乎不占 RAM，不会「翻一倍」。真正该防的是没人查却拖慢每次写的索引。
why_en: This card is only about the MEMORY cost — don't conflate it with the other two. An index has three costs: (1) slower writes — every insert/update/delete must maintain it (write amplification), the main cost; (2) extra disk — a separate B-tree structure; (3) memory — the topic here, and the overhyped one: the buffer pool is an LRU cache that keeps only hot pages, so cold indexes barely occupy RAM (no doubling). The real danger is unused indexes that slow every write for zero read benefit — monitor and drop them.
options_en: Adding one more index directly doubles memory usage.
An index doesn't use even a tiny bit of memory.
Memory impact is the single most damaging cost of an index, the one to worry about first.
The impact is often overstated: buffer pool management is already smart, but index usage still needs monitoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库在内存里缓存磁盘页的区域，减少重复磁盘读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The buffer pool is the in-memory area a database uses to cache disk pages and avoid repeated disk reads.

q_en: Which statement best describes how indexes affect memory usage?
scenario_en: Someone blocks a new index, arguing the server only has 64GB of RAM and every extra index doubles memory usage.

rows: 多一份 B 树结构占盘
每次增删改都要多维护它 → 写变慢
只有被频繁读的热页才进缓冲池

optionExplanations: 夸大了：缓冲池只缓存热页，多数索引躺在盘上不占内存，不会让内存直接翻倍。
索引确实要占一点内存（至少缓存部分热页），说完全不占用是走了另一个极端。
内存不是索引最致命的代价——写放大（每次增删改都要同步维护索引）才是主要成本。
对，缓冲池管理已经很智能，内存影响常被高估；真正要盯的是没人用却拖慢写入的索引，靠监控使用率处理。
optionExplanations_en: Overstated — the buffer pool only caches hot pages, and most of an index sits cold on disk, so memory usage doesn't simply double.
An index does use some memory (at least the hot pages it caches), so claiming zero memory use is the opposite extreme.
Memory isn't the most damaging cost of an index — write amplification (keeping the index in sync on every write) is the main one.
Right — buffer pool management is already smart, so memory impact is often overstated; watch for unused indexes slowing writes instead, via usage monitoring.

scenario: 评审会上要为「这张表再加一个索引」列出全部真实代价，据此决定加还是不加。
q: 给一张表新增一个索引，真实代价有哪些？（多选）
options: 写变慢：每次 INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE 都要顺带更新这个索引（写放大）
占磁盘：索引是表旁边一份独立的 B 树结构，需要额外存储
占内存翻倍：多一个索引，RAM 占用就翻一倍
没人用的索引纯亏：白维护 + 白占盘却零读收益，应监控并删除
why: 加索引两类真实代价：写变慢（每次增删改都要同步维护索引）和占磁盘（独立 B 树结构）。内存常被高估——缓冲池只缓存热页，冷索引几乎不占 RAM。真正要防的是没人查却拖慢写入的索引。
why_en: Adding an index has two real costs: slower writes (every insert/update/delete must maintain it — write amplification, the main one) and extra disk (a separate B-tree). Memory is overhyped: the buffer pool is an LRU cache that keeps only hot pages, so cold indexes barely touch RAM (no doubling). The real danger is unused indexes that slow every write for zero read benefit — monitor and drop them.

rows: 多一份 B 树结构占盘
每次增删改都要多维护它 → 写变慢
只有被频繁读的热页才进缓冲池

q_en: Adding an index to a table has real costs — which are they? (select all that apply)
scenario_en: In a design review you have to list every real cost of adding one more index to this table before deciding to ship it.
options_en: Slower writes: every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE also has to update this index (write amplification).
More disk usage: an index is a separate B-tree structure next to the table, needing extra storage.
Memory usage roughly doubles: adding one more index doubles RAM usage.
An unused index is pure loss: maintained and stored for zero read benefit, so it should be monitored and dropped.
optionExplanations: 写变慢是主要代价：每次 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE 除了改主表，还要同步维护这个索引，拖慢写入吞吐。
占磁盘是实打实的开销：索引是表旁边一份独立的 B 树结构，宽字段索引甚至能接近原表体积。
错——内存占用常被夸大：缓冲池是 LRU 缓存，只留热页在内存，冷索引几乎不占 RAM，不会「翻一倍」。
对，没人用的索引纯亏：白白维护、白占磁盘，读收益是零，应该靠监控使用率定期清理。
optionExplanations_en: Slower writes are the main cost: every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE has to update the main table plus keep this index in sync, dragging down write throughput.
Extra disk usage is a real cost too — an index is a separate B-tree structure next to the table, and on wide columns it can approach the table's own size.
Wrong — the memory hit is often overstated: the buffer pool only keeps hot pages resident, so a cold index barely touches RAM; it doesn't double usage.
Right — an unused index is pure loss: it's maintained and stored for zero read benefit, so it should be found via usage monitoring and dropped.

q: 补全面试常考的索引家族：
text: 通用默认用 {{B-tree}}；极端写入负载用 {{LSM tree}} 存储引擎；纯精确匹配用 {{hash}} 索引；经纬度邻近搜索用 {{geospatial}} 索引（如 GeoHash / R-tree）；全文搜索用 {{inverted}} 索引（倒排）。
why: 五类索引各解一类问题：B 树是万金油，LSM 吃写入，哈希只做等值，地理空间管 2D 邻近，倒排管文本。面试先想清楚查询形态再选。
why_en: B-trees are the default, LSM trees serve write-heavy workloads, hash indexes do exact matches, geospatial indexes handle proximity, and inverted indexes power text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写的存储引擎，靠内存缓冲和后台合并优化写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is a storage engine that turns random writes into sequential writes using an in-memory buffer and background merging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引值哈希到桶、再指向行位置的持久化哈希表结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash index is a persistent hashmap that hashes indexed values into buckets pointing to row locations.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

q_en: Fill in the common index families interviewers expect you to know:
text_en: General-purpose default: {{B-tree}}; write-heavy: {{LSM tree}} storage engine; exact-match only: {{hash}} index; lat/lng proximity: {{geospatial}} index (e.g. GeoHash, R-tree); full-text search: {{inverted}} index.

scenario: 索引放在磁盘上，一次磁盘 I/O 就读一整页；你在比二叉树和 B 树谁更省 I/O。
q: B 树节点和二叉树节点的关键区别是？
options: B 树节点和二叉树一样，每个节点最多只能有两个子节点
B 树节点可以有数百个子节点，节点内是有序的键+指针数组
B 树节点只会存储指向子节点的指针，不存储任何键值
B 树虽然名字里带「树」，但本质上根本不是树结构
why: 二叉树每节点最多两个孩子，B 树节点能有数百个孩子，节点内是有序的键+指针数组。扇出大意味着树很矮，找数据只需极少次磁盘读。
why_en: Unlike binary trees, a B-tree node can have hundreds of children with an ordered array of keys and pointers, keeping the tree shallow to minimize disk reads.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Root page"] --> B["Internal page"]
  B --> C["Leaf page"]
  C --> D["Row pointer"]
options_en: A B-tree node is just like a binary tree — at most two children per node.
A B-tree node can have hundreds of children, with an ordered array of keys plus pointers inside the node.
A B-tree node only stores pointers to its children — it stores no key values at all.
Despite the name, a B-tree isn't fundamentally a tree structure at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个节点最多两个子节点的树结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A binary tree is a tree structure where each node has at most two children.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

q_en: What is the key difference between a B-tree node and a binary-tree node?
scenario_en: The index lives on disk where a single I/O reads a whole page, and you're comparing a binary tree against a B-tree on I/O count.
optionExplanations: 说反了：这恰恰是二叉树的定义（最多两个孩子），B 树的扇出远不止两个。
对，B 树节点通常能塞下数百个键+指针，扇出大意味着树很矮，几次磁盘读就能到叶子。
B 树节点既存键也存指向子树的指针，键负责在节点内做范围划分，不是只存指针。
B 树确实是树结构，只是节点更宽、扇出更大，跟二叉树是同一族的变体。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards — that's the definition of a binary tree (at most two children); a B-tree's fanout is far larger.
Right — a B-tree node typically holds hundreds of keys plus pointers; that high fanout keeps the tree shallow, so a lookup takes only a few disk reads.
A B-tree node stores both keys and child pointers — keys are what let it partition ranges within the node, not pointers alone.
A B-tree is genuinely a tree — it just has much wider nodes and higher fanout than a binary tree, but it's the same family.

scenario: 要让 10 亿行表的点查稳定在 3-4 次磁盘读，B 树必须守住哪些结构不变量？
q: B 树的结构性规则包括哪些？（多选）
options: 所有叶子节点必须在同一深度
非根节点通常保持半满到满（约 m/2 到 m 个键）
有 k 个键的内部节点恰好有 k+1 个子节点
节点内的键无需保持有序
why: 选 A/B/C。B 树靠叶子同深保持平衡；节点通常至少半满，避免树变瘦变高；内部节点的 k 个 key 把范围切成 k+1 段。D 错，因为节点内 key 必须有序。
why_en: Choose A/B/C. A B-tree stays balanced by keeping all leaves at the same depth, keeping nodes roughly half-full or fuller, and using k keys in an internal node to split the key space into k+1 child ranges. D is wrong because keys inside a node must stay sorted.
options_en: All leaf nodes must sit at the same depth.
Non-root nodes usually stay between roughly half-full and full, about m/2 to m keys.
An internal node with k keys has exactly k+1 children.
Keys inside a node do not need to stay sorted.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  R["internal node: keys 10 | 20"]
  R --> C0["child 0: < 10"]
  R --> C1["child 1: 10..20"]
  R --> C2["child 2: > 20"]
  C0 --> L0["leaf depth 2"]
  C1 --> L1["leaf depth 2"]
  C2 --> L2["leaf depth 2"]

termDefinitions.meaning: B 树的阶 m 决定节点容量；不同教材有 max keys 或 max children 两种口径，所以面试里记“至少半满、最多装满”更稳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree's order m determines node capacity; textbooks vary between max-keys and max-children conventions, so in interviews remember the practical idea: roughly half-full to full.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非叶子节点，负责用有序 key 把搜索范围分给多个子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An internal node is a non-leaf node that uses sorted keys to route searches to child ranges.

q_en: Which structural rules does a B-tree maintain? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: To keep point lookups on a billion-row table at three or four disk reads, which structural invariants must a B-tree hold?
optionExplanations: 对，所有叶子必须停在同一层，这正是 B 树「自平衡」的定义，避免某条路径特别深。
对，节点半满到满的约束防止树退化成瘦高结构，保证扇出稳定、树高可控。
对，k 个键把节点的取值范围切成 k+1 段，每段对应一个子指针，这就是内部节点的分支逻辑。
错——节点内的键必须保持有序，这样才能靠二分查找快速定位该往哪个子指针走。
optionExplanations_en: Right — every leaf must sit at the same depth; that's literally the definition of B-tree self-balancing, so no path is disproportionately deep.
Right — keeping nodes half-full to full stops the tree from degenerating into something thin and tall, keeping fanout and height predictable.
Right — k keys split a node's range into k+1 segments, each pointing to one child; that's exactly how internal-node branching works.
Wrong — keys inside a node must stay sorted, which is what makes binary search inside the node possible to pick the right child pointer.

q: B 树节点的大小通常被设计成正好匹配什么？
options: 一个数据库页（Postgres 默认 8KB）
一个 CPU 缓存行（64 字节）
一个内存页（4KB 固定）
整个表的大小
why: 数据库在内存和磁盘之间以「页」为单位读写，Postgres 的页默认 8 KB（编译期参数 BLCKSZ，不是硬件常数；MySQL InnoDB 默认 16 KB）。B 树节点对齐一页，一次 I/O 正好读满一个节点，这是后面对比 LSM / 哈希索引 I/O 效率的基准。
why_en: Databases move data between memory and storage in pages; PostgreSQL's page is 8 KB by default (the compile-time BLCKSZ setting, not a hardware constant; InnoDB defaults to 16 KB). Aligning a B-tree node to one page means one I/O reads one full node, the baseline for later LSM and hash-index comparisons.
scenario: 面试官追问：为什么 Postgres 把 B 树节点大小固定设计成这个数字，而不是随便选。
options_en: One database page (8 KB by default in PostgreSQL)
One CPU cache line, sixty-four bytes.
One fixed four-kilobyte memory page.
The size of the entire table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库读写存储的基本单位，Postgres 默认 8KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database page is the basic unit a database reads and writes in storage; PostgreSQL's default is eight kilobytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘的一次读或写操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O, or Input/Output, here means one read or write operation to disk.

termDefinitions.term: CPU 缓存行 / CPU cache line
termDefinitions.meaning: CPU 内部的小容量高速缓存行，一般 64 字节，远小于磁盘页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU cache line is a small, very fast on-chip cache unit, typically 64 bytes, far smaller than a disk page.

q_en: A B-tree node is usually sized to match what unit?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why PostgreSQL sizes B-tree nodes to this number instead of choosing an arbitrary size.

q: PostgreSQL 用 B 树按 id=350 找一条记录，通常需要读多少个磁盘页？
options: 几十页，需要逐层向下一点点慢慢定位
上百页，几乎等同于把整张表从头到尾完整扫描一遍
个位数：约 3 个索引页（根→内部→叶）+ 1 个 heap 页
必须读整张表的每一页才能最终确认
why: 8 KB 页里放整数主键，扇出大约几百。1000 万行 ÷ 每叶几百条 ≈ 几万个叶页，上面一层几十个内部页，再上面就是根——树高 3 层，读 3 个索引页，再按叶子里的 TID 回表读 1 个 heap 页。表到上亿行时树高也只到 4 左右，所以始终是个位数；实际中根和上层页几乎都在 buffer cache 里，物理读更少。
why_en: With integer keys in 8 KB pages the fanout is a few hundred. Ten million rows over a few hundred entries per leaf is tens of thousands of leaves, a few dozen internal pages above them, then the root — height three, so three index pages, plus one heap page fetched by the leaf's TID. Even at hundreds of millions of rows height is about four, so it stays single-digit; in practice the root and upper levels sit in the buffer cache, so physical reads are fewer still.
scenario: 面试官问：一张约 1000 万行的 PostgreSQL 表，按主键 id=350 用 B 树索引找一行，只算从根到叶的索引页（不考虑缓存命中），再加回表，大概要读多少页？
options_en: Dozens of pages, needing to narrow it down layer by layer, slowly.
Hundreds of pages, nearly equivalent to a full scan of the entire table from start to end.
Single digits: about 3 index pages (root → internal → leaf) plus 1 heap page.
The entire table, every page, must be read to be sure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个树节点能指向的子节点数量，扇出越大树越矮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is how many children a tree node can point to; higher fanout means a shallower tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只查一个精确 key 的查询，例如按主键取一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup is a query for one exact key, such as fetching a row by primary key.

q_en: In PostgreSQL, how many disk pages does a B-tree lookup for id=350 usually read?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: for a PostgreSQL table of about 10 million rows, a B-tree primary-key lookup for id=350 — counting index pages from root to leaf (ignoring cache hits) plus the heap fetch — reads roughly how many pages?
optionExplanations: 几十页意味着树按层线性慢慢缩小范围；B 树的扇出很大，用不了几十页就能锁定。
上百页已经接近全表扫描的量级，那是没有索引、逐页扫描才会有的代价，不是有索引后的样子。
对，扇出有几百，1000 万行的树高约 3 层，3 个索引页加 1 个回表的 heap 页，读页数是个位数。
读整张表是没有索引才会发生的最坏情况，有 B 树索引后不需要这么做。
optionExplanations_en: Dozens of pages implies the tree narrows down layer by layer slowly; a B-tree's fanout is high enough to land the target well before that.
Hundreds of pages is already close to full-scan territory — that's the cost of scanning without an index, not an indexed lookup.
Right — with a fanout of a few hundred, ten million rows give a tree about three levels tall: three index pages plus one heap page, a single-digit read count.

scenario_en: You are building a DataDog-style monitoring system: thousands of servers write hundreds of thousands of CPU, memory, and error-count metrics per second; every point must be stored immediately, while reads are rarer and can tolerate slightly higher latency.

scenario: 指标写入服务每秒 10 万条 INSERT，主键是随机 UUID，索引走 B 树。
q: B 树在每秒 10 万级写入下的瓶颈出在哪？
options: 内存空间完全不够，存不下树的根节点数据
每次写要定位叶页、读入、改、写回——随机寻道成瓶颈
树在高并发写入场景下会逐渐失去自身的平衡
键的数量一旦超出限制，就会溢出单个节点并触发频繁分裂
why: O(log n) 只说明很快找到“哪一页要改”。真正贵的是后半段：把散落在磁盘/SSD 各处的小页读进缓存、改成脏页、之后再刷回去；页满了还可能 split。十万级写入会把这些小而分散的页操作放大成随机 I/O 瓶颈。
why_en: O(log n) only means the database quickly finds which page to change. The expensive part comes after that: load scattered small pages, dirty them in cache, flush them back later, and sometimes split full pages. At very high write rates, those scattered page operations become the random I/O bottleneck.
options_en: There isn't nearly enough memory to hold the tree's root node data.
Every write has to locate the leaf page, read it in, modify it, write it back — random seeks become the bottleneck.
Under heavy concurrent writes, the tree gradually loses its own balance.
Once the key count exceeds a limit, it overflows a single node and triggers frequent splits.

B 树是自平衡结构，高并发写入不会让它失去平衡，split/merge 机制会一直维持平衡。

q_en: Fill in the LSM-tree write path:

scenario: LSM 写入先进 memtable；等 memtable 够大后，系统要把它按 key 顺序刷成 SSTable。
scenario_en: In an LSM tree, writes first enter the memtable; when it is large enough, the system flushes it into an SSTable sorted by key.
q: memtable 通常用什么数据结构实现？
options: 无序数组，按插入顺序追加
布隆过滤器，用于快速排除
有序结构，如红黑树或跳表
堆文件，行没有特定顺序
why: 选 C。写入先追加 WAL 保命，再写内存 sorted map：memtable。memtable 因为按 key 有序，写满后 flush 成 SSTable；WAL 只是临时恢复日志。
why_en: Choose C. A write first appends to the WAL for crash recovery, then updates the in-memory sorted map, the memtable. Because the memtable is sorted by key, it can flush into an SSTable; the WAL is only a temporary recovery log.
options_en: An unordered array, appended in insertion order.
A bloom filter, used to quickly rule things out.
A sorted structure such as a red-black tree or skip list.
A heap file, with rows in no particular order.
diagram:
flowchart LR W["writes"] --> M["Memtable
sorted in memory"] M --> G["get(key)"] M --> R["range scan"] M --> F["flush in key order"] F --> S["SSTable
sorted file"]
codeSample:
memtable = SortedMap()  # in RAM; sorted by key
wal = AppendOnlyLog()  # on disk; temporary crash-recovery log

write(key, value):
  # 1. WAL first: if the process crashes, replay this log.
  wal.append("PUT", key, value)

  # 2. Memtable second: latest state, already sorted by key.
  memtable.put(key, value)

flush_memtable():
  frozen = memtable
  memtable = SortedMap()              # new writes use a fresh memtable
  new_sstable = SSTableFile()

  # Memtable becomes the SSTable because it is already sorted.
  for key, value in frozen.items_in_key_order():
    new_sstable.write(key, value)

  new_sstable.fsync()

  # WAL is not converted into an SSTable; it is retired after the SSTable is safe.
  wal.truncate_records_covered_by(new_sstable)

q: 既然写入已进 memtable，为什么每笔写还要追加到 WAL（预写日志）？

保证持久性：内存崩溃丢失，WAL 顺序追加磁盘更快
为了把数据压缩得更小、尽可能占用更少的磁盘空间容量

why_en: Every write is also appended to a write-ahead log on disk for durability, and sequential appends are much faster than random writes.
options_en: To make subsequent reads a bit faster.
To guarantee durability: memory is lost on a crash, and the WAL appends to disk sequentially, which is fast.
To compress the data smaller and take up as little disk space as possible.
To additionally support certain secondary-index query scenarios.

WAL 记的是原始写入日志，不是为了压缩数据，它甚至会额外占用磁盘空间。

optionExplanations_en: WAL exists to survive crash recovery — unrelated to read speed; it doesn't make later reads any faster.
Right — a memtable lives in RAM and vanishes on a crash; the WAL sequentially appends every write to disk as a safety net, and that's cheap.
The WAL records the raw write log, not a compressed form of the data — it actually adds extra disk usage, not less.

An SSTable lives on disk — it's a durable file, not a temporary in-memory cache.

q_en: Why can a key lookup on an LSM tree be slow in the worst case?

q_en: How does a hash index handle hash collisions?
scenario_en: A hash index has a fixed bucket array, and hashing ten million emails inevitably lands several keys in the same bucket.
optionExplanations: 直接丢弃冲突的键会丢数据，任何正确的索引实现都不会这么做。
冲突只需要处理这一条，不需要重建整个索引——这个代价太夸张了。
对，一个桶能挂多条目、链接溢出页，只要哈希函数分布均匀、负载因子合理，平均仍是 O(1)。
转存到 B 树里处理冲突会让哈希索引退化成一个哈希+树的混合体，不是常见的实现方式。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping a colliding key/value pair would lose data — no correct index implementation would do that.
A collision only needs to be handled for that one entry, not by rebuilding the entire index — that cost would be absurd.
Right — a bucket can hold multiple entries and chain to overflow pages; a well-distributed hash and reasonable load factor keep average lookup O(1).
Spilling collisions into a B-tree would turn a hash index into a hash-plus-tree hybrid, not how it's commonly implemented.

scenario: 你给 created_at 建了哈希索引，产品接着要求「查最近 7 天的订单并按时间排序」。
q: 同一个结构让哈希索引快，也让它废——废在哪？
options: 连它最擅长的等值查询也会跟着一起变慢
相似值被打散到不同桶，范围查询和排序都做不了
占用的存储空间会比原表还大出一个数量级
根本没办法处理字符串类型的键，只能处理数字
why: 哈希的意义就是把值均匀打散，于是「相邻」的值天各一方——范围扫描和排序彻底没戏。这正是它输给 B 树的原因。
why_en: The same hashing that makes exact matches fast deliberately scatters similar values across buckets, making range queries and sorting impossible.
options_en: Even the equality lookups it's best at end up slower too.
Similar values get scattered into different buckets, so range queries and sorting are both impossible.
Its storage footprint ends up an order of magnitude bigger than the original table.
It simply can't handle string-typed keys, only numeric ones.

Right — hashing deliberately scatters similar values into different buckets, so range scans and sorting are completely off the table.
A hash index is usually about as compact as an equivalent B-tree index, not an order of magnitude bigger.
Strings hash perfectly fine — a hash index works just as well on string keys; type support isn't the issue here.

scenario: Postgres 上一张表既有等值查询也有范围查询，你在犹豫默认该建哈希还是 B 树。
q: PostgreSQL 支持哈希索引，却不默认使用，官方理由接近哪句话？
options: 哈希索引完全不支持任何事务相关的操作
哈希索引会占用远超预期的额外内存空间
哈希索引在磁盘上从底层存储原理上根本没有办法实现
B 树做等值几乎不输哈希索引，还白送范围与排序
why: 关键是 B 树的 O(log n) 很小：扇出约 500，一页装几百 key，几十亿行也就 3-4 层，顶层多在缓存。真正成本是磁盘 I/O，B 树等值只比哈希慢一丝丝，却白送范围和排序。
why_en: A B-tree's O(log n) is tiny: each node is a page holding hundreds of keys, so even billions of rows are only 3–4 levels deep. Since the real cost is disk I/O (not comparisons) and the top levels stay cached, equality lookups are only marginally slower than a hash — but you also get range and sort for free. Hence Postgres calls hash indexes a solution to a problem we rarely have.
options_en: A hash index doesn't support any transaction-related operations at all.
A hash index uses far more extra memory than you'd expect.
A hash index simply cannot be implemented on disk at the low-level storage-principle level.
B-tree is nearly as fast as a hash index for equality, and it throws in range and sort for free.

错——哈希索引内存开销并不夸张；不默认用它是因为收益太小、还丢了范围能力。
错——磁盘哈希索引完全可实现（PostgreSQL 就内置）；问题只是收益不值当。
对，B 树查找要翻的层数极少——几十亿行也就 3-4 层，等值查找只比哈希慢一丝丝，却多拿到范围和排序能力。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — a hash index still supports transactions; its real limit is no range or sort, not transactions.
Wrong — a hash index is not a memory hog; it just is not worth losing range support for a tiny gain.
Wrong — on-disk hash indexes are entirely implementable (Postgres ships one); the payoff is just too small.
Right — a B-tree needs very few levels to search — even billions of rows means 3-4 levels, so equality lookup is barely slower than hash, and range plus sort come free.

scenario: 所有数据都在内存中的键值查找场景——比如 Redis 的主数据结构、MySQL 的 MEMORY 存储引擎。
q: 为什么这里哈希结构反而是对的？
options: 因为内存里根本没办法搭建出一棵完整的 B 树
全内存没有磁盘 I/O 要迁就，哈希 O(1) 优势兑现
因为哈希表占用的内存空间比 B 树要更少一些
因为这个使用场景本身其实还需要支持范围查询和区间的排序
why: 磁盘上主导成本是 I/O，B 树几乎不输哈希还更全能；纯内存没有 I/O 可挡，哈希 O(1) 优势才真正兑现，这类场景又只需要等值查找。
why_en: Why the winner flips: on disk, I/O dominates and hides hash's O(1) edge, so a B-tree is nearly as fast and more versatile; in pure memory there's no I/O to hide behind, so the O(1) edge finally shows — and this workload is exact-match only, so hash is right. Redis and the MySQL MEMORY engine both default to hash.
whenOtherWins: 数据落磁盘时选 B 树——它对磁盘 I/O 模式的处理效率更高，等值也几乎不慢。
options_en: Because there's supposedly no way to build a complete B-tree structure in memory at all.
With everything in memory there's no disk I/O to dodge, so the hash table's O(1) advantage actually pays off.
Because a hash table supposedly uses less memory than a B-tree would.
Because this use case actually still needs to support range queries and interval sorting.
tradeoff: 内存中等值查找速度 vs 磁盘场景下的范围查询灵活性

This kind of workload (Redis's core structure, MySQL's MEMORY engine) is typically pure equality key-value lookup, no range query need.

scenario: 要给千万家餐厅做邻近搜索，但数据库只有 B 树这种一维有序索引可用。
q: geohash 的核心思想是什么？
options: 把地球投影到平面网格再取模
递归四等分区域并编码，2D 变 1D 字符串
给每个城市或区域分配一个全局唯一的随机数字 ID

why_en: Geohash recursively subdivides the world and base32-encodes the path, turning a 2D location into a 1D string where nearby places usually share a prefix.
options_en: Project the earth onto a flat grid and take a modulo.
Recursively quarter regions and encode them, turning 2D into a 1D string.
Assign each city or region a globally unique random numeric ID.

why: 拿不准就 B 树（等值+范围通吃、各数据库的默认）；空间数据换 geohash 系空间索引，大规模文本搜索换倒排索引。这三板斧覆盖绝大多数索引问题。
why_en: Default to B-trees, switch to a geospatial index like geohash for lat-lng proximity, and use an inverted index for full-text search.
whenOtherWins: 极端写入摄入（指标、日志、IoT）时再引入 LSM 存储引擎的讨论；纯内存等值查找才轮到哈希结构。
options_en: Always answer hash index because it's fastest, no matter what.
Whenever asked, go ask the DBA first.
Reach for Elasticsearch no matter the scenario.
Default to B-trees; exceptions are geospatial for proximity and inverted for full text.
tradeoff: 通用默认覆盖大多数场景 vs 特化索引服务少数场景

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库管理员，负责数据库运维和优化的角色。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DBA stands for Database Administrator, the role responsible for operating and tuning databases.

termDefinitions.term: 地理空间索引 / geospatial index
termDefinitions.meaning: 理解二维空间邻近关系的索引，如 geohash、四叉树、R 树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index understands 2D proximity, implemented via approaches like geohash, quadtrees, or R-trees.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「词 → 包含它的文档列表」反向存储的索引，支撑全文搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index stores a mapping from each word to the list of documents containing it, powering full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种自平衡的多路搜索树，节点可以有多个子节点，保持数据有序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a self-balancing multi-way search tree that keeps data sorted with many children per node.

q_en: What is the right default decision flow for choosing an index type?
scenario_en: In an interview, you are asked which index type fits a scenario and need a one-sentence general decision rule.
optionExplanations: 把哈希索引当默认答案风险很高——一旦场景需要范围查询或排序，这个答案立刻站不住。
面试现场没有 DBA 可问，面试官想看的是你自己能不能推出一个合理默认，不是回避决策。
Elasticsearch 是为全文搜索定制的重型方案，普通等值/范围查询场景直接上它是杀鸡用牛刀。
对，拿不准先默认 B 树；邻近查询换地理空间索引，全文检索换倒排索引，这三板斧覆盖了大多数场景。
optionExplanations_en: Treating a hash index as the default answer is risky — the moment the scenario needs range queries or sorting, that answer falls apart.
There's no DBA to ask in an interview — the interviewer wants to see you reason your way to a sensible default yourself, not dodge the decision.
Elasticsearch is a heavyweight tool purpose-built for full-text search — reaching for it on an ordinary equality/range query is overkill.
Right — default to B-tree when unsure; swap to a geospatial index for proximity queries and an inverted index for full-text search.

scenario: DynamoDB 聊天表按 user_id 分区，最常见的查询是「查某个用户在某时间段内的消息」，需要按时间区间取。
scenario_en: A DynamoDB chat table is partitioned by user_id, and the hottest query is 'a given user's messages in a time window', needing a time range.
q: 怎么建模才能让「单用户 + 时间区间」这类查询走连续扫描？
q_en: How do you model the table so a single-user time-range query becomes a contiguous scan?
options: 把 timestamp 设为该表的 sort key，让分区内 item 有序
另建一个只以 timestamp 为键的 GSI，靠它做时间区间扫描
依赖底层 B 树索引，直接对 timestamp 列做范围扫描
用 Scan 把整个分区读出来，再用 FilterExpression 过滤掉区间外的项
options_en: Make timestamp the table's sort key so items within the partition are stored in order.
Build a separate GSI keyed only on timestamp and use it for the time-range scan.
Rely on the underlying B-tree index to range-scan the timestamp column directly.
Use Scan to read the whole partition, then FilterExpression to drop items outside the window.
why: 同分区内 item 按 sort key 有序存放，所以「固定 partition key + sort key 区间」是一次连续读，代价接近顺序扫描。代价：这份有序只在单个 partition key 内成立。
why_en: DynamoDB keeps items within a partition ordered by sort key, so a fixed partition key plus a sort-key range is one contiguous read, close to a sequential scan in cost. The catch: that ordering only holds inside a single partition key.
whenOtherWins: 当查询不带 user_id、要跨所有用户按时间全局排序或取区间时，分区内 sort key 帮不上，得建一个以 time 为分区/排序键的 GSI。
tradeoff: 分区内 sort-key 区间（单分区有序、最省）vs GSI（跨分区但另建结构）vs Scan（全读再过滤）

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 复合主键的第二部分；同一 partition key 下的 item 按 sort key 有序存放，因此支持分区内区间查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The sort key is the second part of a DynamoDB composite primary key; items under one partition key are stored in sort-key order, enabling in-partition range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复合主键的第一部分，决定 item 落在哪个物理分区；有序区间查询只在同一个 partition key 内成立。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the first part of the primary key and decides which physical partition an item lands in; ordered range queries only hold within one partition key.

termDefinitions.fullName: Global Secondary Index（全局二级索引）
termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用另一套键（可跨分区）重新组织数据的附加索引，供主键之外的查询模式使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GSI is an extra DynamoDB index that reorganizes data under a different key, possibly across partitions, for query patterns beyond the primary key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 追加写、后台合并的存储结构；DynamoDB 被普遍认为用 LSM 式底座而非 B 树，因此没有用户可范围扫描的 B 树索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is an append-and-merge storage structure; DynamoDB is widely understood to use an LSM-style engine rather than B-trees, so there is no user-facing B-tree to range-scan.

termDefinitions.meaning: Scan 读遍整张表或整个分区，FilterExpression 只在读完之后丢弃不匹配项——不减少读取量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scan reads the whole table or partition, and FilterExpression only discards non-matching items after reading — it does not reduce how much is read.

optionExplanations: 对，这正是把 timestamp 放进 sort key 的目的：同一 user_id 下的时间区间落成一段相邻磁盘读，而非逐条随机点查。
以 timestamp 为键的 GSI 是把数据跨分区重排，适合「跨用户按时间查」，但对「单用户区间」是绕远路。
DynamoDB 被普遍认为用 LSM 式底座、不是 B 树，没有可供用户对 timestamp 做范围扫描的 B 树索引。
Scan 会把整个分区都读出来再过滤，读取量不随区间收窄——正是 sort key 有序想避免的浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Right — items sit in sort-key order within the partition, so a fixed user_id plus a timestamp range is one contiguous read.
A GSI keyed on timestamp reorders data across partitions, good for 'time across all users' but a detour for a single user's range.
DynamoDB is understood to use an LSM-style engine, not B-trees, so there's no user B-tree to range-scan on timestamp.
Scan reads the entire partition then filters, so the read volume doesn't shrink with the window — the waste sort-key ordering avoids.

scenario: 用四叉树（把二维空间递归四等分的树）做「找我附近 1 公里的餐厅」，你已经下钻到自己所在的叶象限。
scenario_en: Using a quadtree (a tree that recursively quarters 2D space) for 'restaurants within 1 km of me', you've drilled down to your own leaf quadrant.
q: 为什么只返回这个叶象限里的点会漏掉最近的餐厅？
q_en: Why does returning only the points inside this leaf quadrant miss the nearest restaurant?
options: 最近的点可能就贴在象限边界另一侧的相邻象限里
本象限里的点没有按到我的距离排好序，结果顺序是乱的
四叉树不平衡，我所在的这个叶象限有可能恰好是空的
象限用 geohash 字符串编号，前缀比较有时会把邻居判成远点
options_en: The nearest point may sit just across the boundary in an adjacent quadrant.
Points in this quadrant aren't sorted by distance to me, so the order is scrambled.
A quadtree is unbalanced, so my leaf quadrant might happen to be empty.
Quadrants are labeled by geohash strings, and prefix comparison sometimes misjudges neighbors as far.
why: 下钻只覆盖了一块方格，真正的最近邻可能落在紧贴边界的相邻象限。所以邻近查询要走完整链：定位目标象限 → 检查同层相邻象限 → 按搜索半径上钻覆盖更大范围或下钻更精细。代价：一次邻近查询要触碰多个象限节点，不是单点查找。
why_en: Drilling down only covers one cell, but the true nearest neighbor can fall in an adjacent quadrant hugging the boundary. So a proximity search runs the full loop: find the target quadrant, check same-level neighbors, then move up or down levels by the search radius. The cost: one query touches several quadrant nodes, not a single lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维空间递归四等分成象限的树；点太密就继续四分，稀疏区保留大格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadtree is a tree that recursively splits 2D space into four quadrants; dense areas keep subdividing while sparse areas keep large cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 四叉树一次四等分得到的一块方格区域，对应树里的一个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quadrant is one of the four cells produced by a quadtree split, corresponding to one node in the tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 找「距某点半径内的所有对象」的查询；在四叉树里需要跨相邻象限、按半径调层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proximity search finds all objects within a radius of a point; in a quadtree it must cross neighboring quadrants and adjust levels by radius.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把二维坐标编码成保留邻近性的字符串（另一种空间索引路线），靠前缀匹配做邻近查询——不是四叉树的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Geohash encodes 2D coordinates into a proximity-preserving string (a different spatial-index path) and uses prefix matching, not the quadtree's mechanism.

optionExplanations: 对，边界是人为切的，最近邻可能就在隔壁象限，所以必须再查同层相邻象限并按半径调层。
排序不是问题——问题是完整性：漏了相邻象限里更近的点，排不排序都补不回来。
四叉树按点密度自适应细分，空象限不是漏点的原因；漏点来自没查边界外的邻居。
把坐标编成前缀字符串是 geohash 的做法；四叉树直接切分空间、用树导航，不靠前缀比较。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the boundary is arbitrary, the nearest neighbor may be next door, so you must also check same-level neighbors and adjust levels by radius.
Ordering isn't the issue — completeness is: a closer point in an adjacent quadrant is missed whether or not you sort.
A quadtree subdivides adaptively by point density; an empty quadrant isn't why points are missed — skipping boundary neighbors is.
Encoding coordinates into prefix strings is geohash's approach; a quadtree partitions space directly and navigates the tree, not by prefixes.

scenario: 线上一个查询突然变慢，表上已经有几个索引，团队不确定到底该给哪列再加索引。
scenario_en: A production query suddenly got slow; the table already has a few indexes, and the team isn't sure which column to index next.
q: 定位「该加什么索引」的第一步应该是什么？
q_en: What should the first step be to figure out which index to add?
options: 跑 EXPLAIN 看查询计划，确认它卡在哪个谓词、有没有 seq scan
给 WHERE 子句里出现的每一列都单独建一个索引，用数量硬覆盖所有过滤组合
按表的行数决定：行多就加索引，行少就先不加
直接把表迁到写入更快的 LSM 引擎上
options_en: Run EXPLAIN to read the query plan and see which predicate it stalls on and whether it's doing a seq scan.
Add an index to every column that appears in the WHERE clause to cover all possibilities.
Decide by row count: index if the table is big, skip it if the table is small.
Migrate the table onto an LSM engine that writes faster.
why: 索引不是免费的——每建一个都加写放大和存储，盲目加还可能既不命中慢查询又拖慢写入。先用 EXPLAIN/查询计划加数据库指标找到真正的瓶颈谓词，再针对性建索引。代价：多一步诊断，换来不建无效索引。
why_en: Indexes aren't free — each one adds write amplification and storage, and blind ones may miss the slow query while slowing writes. First use EXPLAIN plus database metrics to find the real bottleneck predicate, then index for it. The cost: one extra diagnosis step, in exchange for not building dead indexes.
whenOtherWins: 当查询模式一开始就明确（例如登录永远按 email 精确匹配），建表时直接把索引建好即可，不必先跑 EXPLAIN 诊断。
tradeoff: 先诊断后建索引（多一步、只加有用的）vs 盲目全列建索引（省诊断、堆写入成本）

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库命令，打印某条查询的执行计划——它打算用哪些索引、要不要全表扫描、各步预估代价。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPLAIN is a database command that prints a query's execution plan — which indexes it will use, whether it will scan the whole table, and the estimated cost of each step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库为一条查询选定的执行方案（用哪个索引、按什么顺序连接、扫描方式），是判断瓶颈的入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query plan is the execution strategy the database picks for a query — which index, join order, and scan method — and is the entry point for spotting bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Sequential scan，数据库逐行读遍整张表；查询计划里出现它往往意味着某个谓词缺可用索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A seq (sequential) scan reads every row of the table in order; seeing it in a plan often means a predicate lacks a usable index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询里的过滤条件（如 WHERE user_id=123）；诊断的目标是找出哪个谓词没走索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A predicate is a filter condition in a query (like WHERE user_id=123); diagnosis aims to find which predicate isn't using an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写入被放大成多次物理写：每多一个索引，插入/更新就要多改一份结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is one logical write turning into several physical writes: each extra index means an insert or update must modify one more structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向高写入的追加写存储结构；换引擎解决的是写吞吐，不是「哪列该建索引」的读诊断问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree is an append-oriented storage structure for high write throughput; switching engines addresses write throughput, not the read-side question of which column to index.

optionExplanations: 对，先看查询计划才知道慢在哪个谓词、是不是在做 seq scan，再据此选列建索引最省。
给每列都建索引会堆高写放大和存储，还可能建了一堆没命中慢查询的死索引。
行数只是粗略信号——真正决定要不要索引的是访问模式，光看大小会误判。
换 LSM 引擎解决的是写吞吐，和「哪个读谓词缺索引」是两根轴，跑偏了。
optionExplanations_en: Right — read the plan first to see which predicate is slow and whether it's a seq scan, then index that column.
Indexing every column piles on write amplification and storage, and may create dead indexes that never hit the slow query.
Row count is only a rough signal — access pattern decides whether an index helps; size alone misleads.
Switching to LSM addresses write throughput, a different axis from which read predicate lacks an index.
